title: New Research Shows Midlife Health Habits Can Delay Dementia
subtitle: Managing three specific health factors between ages 45 and 65 may help people live over a decade longer without brain-related decline.

summary.en: A new study published in the journal Neurology suggests that midlife health choices significantly impact brain health in later years. Researchers found that avoiding smoking, high blood pressure, and type 2 diabetes can add nearly 13 years of dementia-free life. The study followed over 12,000 participants for about 30 years to track these outcomes. Experts emphasize that heart health is closely connected to brain health. These findings offer hope that many cases of dementia can be delayed through early lifestyle management.
summary.zh: 發表在《神經學》期刊上的一項新研究顯示，中年時期的健康選擇會顯著影響晚年的腦部健康。研究人員發現，避免抽菸、高血壓和第二型糖尿病，可以增加近十三年沒有失智症的健康生活。該研究追蹤了超過一萬二千名參與者約三十年，以觀察這些結果。專家強調，心臟健康與腦部健康密切相關。這些發現帶來了希望，顯示透過及早管理生活方式，許多失智症病例是可以延緩的。

paragraphs.en: A major new study has identified three key health factors during middle age that could help people live without dementia for more than a decade longer. According to The Guardian Health, researchers found that keeping blood pressure at a normal level, avoiding type 2 diabetes, and not smoking between the ages of 45 and 65 are strongly linked to a longer, healthier life. Dementia is a general term for a decline in brain function that makes it difficult to remember things or think clearly. As the global population ages, the number of people living with this condition is expected to reach 153 million by 2050. However, experts believe that many of these cases could be delayed or prevented by focusing on health early in life.
paragraphs.zh: 一項重大的新研究指出，中年時期的三個關鍵健康因素，能幫助人們延長超過十年的失智症無症狀生活。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，研究人員發現，在四十五歲至六十五歲之間維持正常血壓、避免罹患第二型糖尿病以及不抽菸，與更長壽且更健康的生活有強烈關聯。失智症是腦部功能衰退的統稱，會導致記憶力減退或思考能力下降。隨著全球人口老化，預計到二〇五〇年，罹患此症的人數將達到一億五千三百萬人。然而，專家認為，若能及早關注健康，許多病例是可以延緩或預防的。

paragraphs.en: The research, published in the medical journal Neurology, was conducted by scientists at NYU Langone Health. They looked at data from a long-term study that followed thousands of Americans starting in 1986. The team examined 12,409 people who were free of dementia at the start of the study, with an average age of 56. Over the next 26 years, the researchers tracked the health of these participants. They discovered that those who had none of the three risk factors lived almost 13 years longer without developing dementia compared to those who had all three.
paragraphs.zh: 這項發表在醫學期刊《神經學》（Neurology）上的研究，是由紐約大學朗格尼醫學中心（NYU Langone Health）的科學家所進行。他們分析了一項自一九八六年開始、追蹤數千名美國人的長期研究數據。研究團隊檢視了一萬二千四百零九名在研究開始時並未罹患失智症的受試者，其平均年齡為五十六歲。在接下來的二十六年裡，研究人員持續追蹤這些參與者的健康狀況。他們發現，與三項風險因素皆具備的人相比，完全沒有這三項風險因素的人，能多出近十三年的失智症無症狀生活。

paragraphs.en: The findings show a clear connection between midlife habits and later brain health. People who started the study with no diabetes, no high blood pressure, and who did not smoke had an average of 30.1 more years free of dementia. Those with one risk factor had about 26 years, while those with two had 21 years. People who had all three risk factors had the lowest number of dementia-free years, at just over 17. Dr. Josef Coresh, a senior investigator at NYU Langone, stated that these findings show people should actively manage these health factors starting at age 45 to protect their brain health for the future.
paragraphs.zh: 研究結果顯示，中年習慣與晚年腦部健康之間存在明確的關聯。在研究開始時沒有糖尿病、沒有高血壓且不抽菸的人，平均能多出三十點一年沒有失智症的健康生活。具備一項風險因素的人約有二十六年，而具備兩項的人則有二十一年。具備全部三項風險因素的人，其無失智症的年數最少，僅略高於十七年。紐約大學朗格尼醫學中心資深研究員柯瑞許博士（Dr. Josef Coresh）表示，這些發現顯示人們應從四十五歲開始積極管理這些健康因素，以保護未來的腦部健康。

paragraphs.en: While the study provides a clear path for prevention, it also noted differences among groups. The research suggested that, regardless of the number of risk factors, women generally lived longer without dementia than men. It also found that white participants had more dementia-free years than black participants. These differences highlight that while lifestyle choices are important, other factors may also play a role in how long people stay healthy. The study authors noted that these three risk factors often appear in middle age and have a lasting effect on the brain, which is why identifying and treating them early is so important.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然這項研究為預防失智症提供了明確的方向，但也指出了不同群體之間的差異。研究顯示，無論風險因素的多寡，女性通常比男性擁有更長的無失智症生活年數。研究也發現，白人參與者的無失智症年數多於黑人參與者。這些差異凸顯出，儘管生活方式的選擇很重要，但其他因素也可能影響人們保持健康的時長。研究作者指出，這三項風險因素通常在中年時期出現，並對大腦產生持久影響，這就是為什麼及早識別並治療它們如此重要的原因。

paragraphs.en: Experts who were not involved in the study have praised the research for its practical approach. Dr. Jacqui Hanley, head of research funding at Alzheimer’s Research UK, noted that the study asks a question that matters to everyone: how many years can we expect to live without dementia? She explained that this approach helps people understand how their current health choices shape their future. According to The Guardian Health, Dr. Hanley emphasized that the findings show why it is vital to look after heart health to protect the brain. She recommended that everyone take practical steps, such as staying physically active and managing conditions like high blood pressure and diabetes, to improve their long-term health.
paragraphs.zh: 未參與此項研究的專家們稱讚該研究採取了務實的方法。英國阿茲海默症研究中心（Alzheimer’s Research UK）的研究資助負責人漢利博士（Dr. Jacqui Hanley）指出，這項研究提出了一個與每個人息息相關的問題：我們預期能有多少年是不受失智症困擾的？她解釋說，這種方法有助於人們理解目前的健康選擇如何塑造未來。根據《衛報健康》報導，漢利博士強調，這些發現顯示了照顧心臟健康以保護大腦的重要性。她建議每個人都應採取實際行動，例如保持身體活動，並管理高血壓和糖尿病等疾病，以改善長期的健康狀況。

paragraphs.en: This research adds to a growing body of evidence about how to prevent brain decline. Previous studies have suggested that addressing 14 different risk factors throughout a person’s life—starting from childhood—could prevent or delay 45% of dementia cases worldwide. The new findings from NYU Langone Health reinforce the idea that it is never too early to start caring for your health. By focusing on these three specific areas during middle age, individuals may be able to significantly increase the number of years they spend living a healthy, active life. As medical science continues to advance, the focus remains on helping people understand that their daily habits are powerful tools for protecting their future well-being.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究為如何預防腦部衰退提供了更多證據。先前的研究曾建議，從童年開始處理人一生中十四種不同的風險因素，可以預防或延緩全球百分之四十五的失智症病例。來自紐約大學朗格尼醫學中心的新發現強化了一個觀念：開始照顧健康永遠不嫌早。透過在中年時期專注於這三個特定領域，個人或許能顯著增加過著健康、活躍生活的年數。隨著醫學持續進步，重點依然在於幫助人們理解，他們的日常習慣是保護未來福祉的強大工具。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Without or not containing something, especially something unpleasant.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 沒有（某種負面事物）的；免於……的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 容易誤以為是「免費」，但在這裡表示「沒有、不受影響」。文中：The team examined 12,409 people who were free of dementia at the start of the study, with an average age of 56.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To monitor or follow the progress or development of someone or something over a period of time.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（足跡、軌道），這裡作動詞，指長期觀察研究對象。文中：Over the next 26 years, the researchers tracked the health of these participants.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To influence the way that a situation or person develops.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（形狀），這裡作動詞，指影響未來發展。文中：She explained that this approach helps people understand how their current health choices shape their future.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A collection or group of things, such as evidence or information.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（身體），這裡指研究證據的累積總量。文中：This research adds to a growing body of evidence about how to prevent brain decline.

quiz.question: According to the study, how many dementia-free years did participants with all three risk factors experience on average?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，研究指出擁有全部三項風險因子（糖尿病、高血壓、吸菸）的參與者，其無失智症生存年數僅「剛好超過 17 年」(just over 17)。選項 A 的 13 年是兩組人之間的差距而非總年數；選項 C 是擁有兩項風險因子的數據；選項 D 則是完全沒有風險因子者的數據，故皆錯誤。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between heart health and brain health based on the text?

options.A: Heart health is the only factor that determines whether a person will develop dementia.
options.B: The brain is unaffected by physical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
options.C: Maintaining a healthy heart is a recommended strategy for preserving cognitive function.
options.D: Medical experts believe that dementia is purely a genetic condition that cannot be managed.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第五段，Dr. Jacqui Hanley 強調研究結果顯示「照顧心臟健康對於保護大腦至關重要」(vital to look after heart health to protect the brain)。由此可推論，心血管健康與大腦功能息息相關。選項 A 過度推論，文中提到還有其他風險因子；選項 B 與文中證據矛盾；選項 D 則與文章強調「生活習慣能預防失智」的主旨完全相反。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'reinforce' mean in the context of the sentence: 'The new findings from NYU Langone Health reinforce the idea that it is never too early to start caring for your health.'?

options.A: To weaken or challenge an existing belief
options.B: To strengthen or support an existing idea
options.C: To replace an old theory with a new one

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，reinforce 的意思是「加強」或「鞏固」。這項新發現證實了先前關於健康習慣重要性的觀點，使其更有說服力。選項 A 與原意相反；選項 C 錯誤，因為研究是「補充」而非「取代」舊有理論；選項 D 則完全曲解了 reinforce 的用法與文章語意。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: Lifestyle choices in middle age can significantly impact the number of years lived without dementia.
options.B: Medical science has finally discovered a permanent cure for all types of dementia.
options.C: The global population is aging faster than researchers previously predicted.
options.D: Genetic factors are more important than lifestyle choices in preventing brain decline.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。全文核心在於探討中年時期針對血壓、糖尿病與吸菸這三項風險因子進行管理，能有效延長無失智症的健康生活年數。選項 B 文中並未提及「永久治癒」；選項 C 雖然在第一段提到人口老化，但僅為背景資訊而非主旨；選項 D 與文章強調「生活習慣的重要性」相悖，故 A 最能涵蓋全文重點。
